runconfig-resolver.problem: The Serial-vs-MT decision and the "macro/" + argv[1]-or-beam.in fallback are plain statements interleaved with G4RunManagerFactory calls inside main, with no seam a test can enter through.
runconfig-resolver.solution: Extract a pure ResolveRunConfig(argc, argv) returning {type, threads, macroFile}; main calls it once, then wires Geant4 objects from the result.
runconfig-resolver.benefits: Leverage: first module in the project testable without a Geant4 runtime. Locality: the "which macro, how many threads" question moves from a scan of main to one function signature.

gui-batch-seam.problem: GUI and batch are two real adapters of how the run executes, but today they're an inline if/else in main with manual new/delete resource management duplicated only in the GUI branch.
gui-batch-seam.solution: Give them a shared Run(mode, UIManager) seam with an interactive adapter and a batch adapter, each owning its own resource lifetimes.
gui-batch-seam.benefits: Tension flagged: useGUI is a hardcoded compile-time flag with one caller per binary, a hypothetical seam per CLAUDE.md's no-extra-abstraction rule -- only worth it if GUI mode sees real use beyond occasional debugging.

remove-dead-out-global.problem: File-scope std::ofstream out; has no reader or writer anywhere in src/ -- ScoreSpecies.cc declares its own unrelated local out for Species.Txt.
remove-dead-out-global.solution: Delete the dead global. Previously flagged 'leave alone for now' in .claude/plan-class-based-chemistry.md, but that note predates this file's new --threads/MT support, which makes an eventual accidental write to it a real data race rather than a hypothetical one.
remove-dead-out-global.benefits: Deletion test says delete: nothing reads this global, and no seam is being served by keeping it.
